variables.E: The residence time distribution (RTD) of the fluid, represented by the E(t) curve

context_text: In order to analyze the residence time distribution of the fluid in a reactor the following relationships have been developed. Fluid elements may require differing lengths of time to travel through the reactor. The distribution of the exit times, defined as the E(t) curve, is the residence time distribution (RTD) of the fluid. This equation represents the normalization of the distribution.

variables.C_f: Magnitude of the step input concentration

context_text: With a step input of magnitude C_f, this equation represents the unsteady material balance for a CSTR. The ODE is linear, allowing for solutions by Laplace transforms.

variables.F(t_r): Cumulative distribution function of residence time

context_text: This equation is the integral of the unsteady material balance (Equation 1.2) for a step input. It represents the normalized concentration response over time, also known as the F-curve.
With an impulse input of magnitude m or an initial mean concentration C^0 = m/V_r, this equation represents the material balance for the tracer in the CSTR.
This equation is the solution to the material balance for a pulse input (Equation 1.4) and represents the ideal Residence Time Distribution (E-curve) for a CSTR.

This equation shows the relationship between the residence time distribution function (E-curve), which is the response to a pulse input, and the cumulative distribution function (F-curve), which is the response to a step input.
